 bleed_attack_bonus : The Bleed Attack Bonus (abbreviated as Bleed BNS in-game) increases the amount of Bleed buildup inflicted per hit. It does not affect the total amount of damage the Bleed effect will do. Unlike weapons that have a magical scaling stat, Bleed has no equivalent scaling.

The Bleed BNS value is determined by the Dexterity and Faith stats. In order to continually increase innate Bleed BNS, both Dexterity and Faith need to be leveled up, with Dexterity giving a larger bonus.

title: Bleed (Dark Souls II)

 infusion : Steady Hand McDuff can infuse most weapons with Bleed through the use of a Bleed Stone. Once a weapon is infused, the Bleed icon () will be displayed next to its image in the HUD.

Uninfused weapons imbued with Bleed gain a fixed Bleed buildup value (which does **not** scale with the Bleed Attack Bonus), but the base physical damage is lowered by 30%. For example, if a regular weapon that deals 100 physical damage is infused with Bleed, its stats switch over to 70 physical damage and 112 Bleed buildup.
Weapons with innate Bleed buildup gain an additional increase to Bleed buildup, but the base physical damage is lowered by 5%, as is the current scaling. For example, the Bandit's Knife goes from 65 physical damage + 67 Bleed buildup to 62 physical damage + 96 Bleed buildup when infused.
Shields gain additional Bleed resistance while lowering other resistances.

The rate at which this fills is dependent on the Bleed buildup value of the attacker's weapon or item; and the target's Bleed Resist stat. Gold Pine Bundle -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Unlike resins, which require the user to remain stationary while applying the buff, bundles take less than a second to activate and can be used while moving. While they grant more damage than their respective resins and many more bundles can be carried at once, the trade-off is that the duration of the buff is reduced to less than 20% of that of a resin.

The quick application time, high stock and low duration of these items makes them very flexible tools, useful for applying in the midst of combat based on the situation. Whereas a resin may find a large fraction of its duration wasted from inactivity between attacks, a bundle may be quickly activated when an opportunity to deal damage presents itself, and the advantage pressed until the buff expires. Usually this is expressed as a percentage of the catalyst's Spell Buff, which is then directly added to the weapon's attack power.

In the case of special catalysts that scale with more than one stat or which scale with an unusual stat (such as Man-grub's Staff and Crystal Chime, the effectiveness of the weapon buff is severely weakened. In the case of off-stat catalysts a flat 100 Spell Buff is used in the calculation, while in the case of dual-scaling catalysts only the half of the Spell Buff which is normally associated with the spell is used in the calculation.

snippet:

 lead : **Waterlogged** is a status effect in *Dark Souls II*.

It is contracted when standing in a Pharros' Contraption that fills an empty pool with healing water, or patches of water found in many areas of the game. The healing water slowly regenerates health as the player stands in it, and cures status effects like poison by allowing it to wash off. This effect also works like the Flash Sweat pyromancy, making the player far more resistant to fire attacks, at the cost of taking more lightning damage. The effect can also stack with Flash Sweat for even more fire defense.

In some areas of the game, this can occur automatically, such as traversing water itself, or during a rain storm. However, this will not regenerate the player's health, but instead only alter their elemental resistances. Care should be taken as to who or what the player is going to fight when the status effect is contracted.

Bows can be equipped in either the left or right hand weapon slots. Because the player is required to hold the bow with both hands to fire, the Strength requirement can be circumvented.

All bows have a "zoom" feature that allows the player to get a closer look at their aim point. It should be noted that different types of Arrows have different ranges that add to a specific bow's range. This affects the accuracy of the projectile resulting in some shots seeming inaccurate (this does not affect locked-on shots). Range can also be increased by equipping the Hawk Ring.

snippet:

 characteristics : A favorite in PvP, the Red Hilted Halberd can be a very strong polearm in the right hands.

Utilizing the thrusting halberd moveset, the Red Hilted Halberd is generally incapable of taking advantage of Hyper Armor except when performing a two-handed strong attack, which has a long wind-up and leaves the wielder wide open if it misses. Compared to the normal Halberd, it performs better with physical infusions but is weaker than its cousin when it comes to elemental infusions.

What makes this weapon useful, however, is that it is the only halberd in the game with Perseverance, which grants the wielder passive Poise while also reducing any incoming damage. This means that unlike most other halberds, the Red Hilted Halberd has an option to stand its ground and fight enemies head-on if they manage to get inside of the weapon's reach.

title: Barbed Straight Sword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Barbed Straight Sword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Barbed Straight Sword shares the same moveset as the Long Sword, except each successful attack also causes bleed build-up, which upon infliction, will take off a sizable portion of an enemy's HP.

It is able to be buffed with both resins and spells.

As a note, the strong attack whilst in Stance will cause notably more bleed build-up if the attack connects with the target.

title: Elemental Damage
snippet:
Elemental Damage -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : In *Dark Souls II*, a new elemental damage type in the form of Dark has been added, as well as the Hexes school of casting. All forms of elemental damage are tied to how Intelligence and Faith are leveled up, with different amounts of effectiveness depending on the stat spread. Magic is tied to Intelligence, Lightning is tied to Faith, while Fire is tied to the sum of both, and Dark is tied to the lower of both.

title: Equipment (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Equipment (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - weapons 
 weapons : Weapons will be one of the main sources of damage for most players. These items come in all different shapes and sizes, ranging from Daggers to Great Hammers. All weapons can be parried, leaving the player open for a riposte, which is one of the most damaging forms of critical attack. Weapons can also be infused with different elements and status effects, typically lowering the damage scaling but increasing the effectiveness of that element or status effect.

title: Untrue Dark Ring
snippet:
Untrue Dark Ring -  Dark Souls III - ring - effect 
 effect : Makes the wearer always have human appearance and removes the phantom glow when they are summoned or are invading. Secondarily, it also hides the burning effect from the wearer's attire when a Host of Embers, and the glow of weapons reinforced with certain spells, items or skills. The particle effects coming from the wearer and it's weapon still remain.

title: Crest Shield (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Crest Shield (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : One of two returning crest shields from *Dark Souls* and one of the four enchanted blue shields in *Dark Souls III*, the Crest Shield specializes in blocking Dark damage.

Besides its respectable elemental absorptions across the board, it possesses the highest Dark absorption out of all shields in the game, short of Deep infusions on certain shields. As a medium shield, it has a low Strength requirement and possesses moderate weight and stability, as well as blocking 100% of physical damage, making it a good general-purpose shield.

title: Strong Magic Shield (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Strong Magic Shield (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - spell - effect 
 effect : This sorcery can be cast on any shield to imbue it with Magic, similar to infusions. This grants the shield a 100% defense against all types of attacks (including Magic, physical and some status effects) when blocking, while increasing stability by 10% (this effect stacks with that of the Baneful Bird Ring). The duration of this spell ranges from 21 seconds when the spell is spiced down to 10 Intelligence all the way up to 60 seconds at 27 Intelligence where the duration scaling caps.

title: Rapport
snippet:

title: Halberd (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Compared to the only other thrusting halberd in the game, the Red Hilted Halberd, the normal Halberd possesses different scaling values as well as a different skill. Whereas the Red Hilted Halberd can perform Perseverance and engage foes head-on, the normal Halberd possesses a Charge attack that can be useful for Poise trades or for running down fleeing targets. In terms of damage, the Red Hilted Halberd is stronger when it comes to infusions that enhance physical attributes, particularly the Sharp infusion. However, when infused down the elemental path such as with a Lightning Gem, the normal Halberd has superior performance.

title: Buildup
snippet:
Buildup -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : The term **Buildup** in *Dark Souls* is specific to auxiliary effects. It refers to the bar that appears on screen when a player character receives a specific effect. When the bar is "full", the character is subject to the effect.

title: Drakeblood Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Overall, the Drakeblood Greatsword possesses many intrinsic advantages that makes it very strong in the hands of a build that does not prioritize physical damage. Its innate elemental damage, combined with its ability to be buffed or infused, make it a force to be reckoned with when buffed with Lightning Blade, Darkmoon Blade or Crystal Magic Weapon, or when infused with any number of elemental gems to amplify its damage output.

title: Shield of the Insolent

The clerics held venerated positions once, but now, their souls wander aimlessly in the depths of a murky darkness.

title: Negative Status Effects
snippet:
Negative Status Effects -  Dark Souls - mechanic - bleed_dark_souls_bleed 
 bleed_dark_souls_bleed : Bleed is a status effect that builds up after successive attacks from specific enemies' weapons. Once the bleed meter is full, it will deal damage based on a percentage of the victim's health. Taking too many bleed effects can become fatal very quickly. Bleed build-up can be stopped through use of a Bloodred Moss Clump, a Divine Blessing, or with the sorcery Remedy.

Bleed damage can be avoided by rolling the moment when the bleed meter fills.

title: Dark Hand (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Dark Hand (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Returning from the first game, the Dark Hand can be useful as an early-game weapon but otherwise functions as a utility tool.

Unlike other fist weapons, the Dark Hand is not paired, and it cannot be two-handed. Wielding the weapon in different hands results in different movesets. In the right-hand, it functions as a one-handed fist weapon, performing various close-combat attacks; in the left-hand, it can be used to project a shield that has high elemental defense but low stability, making it ideal for protecting the wielder against projectile spells, as well as perform a unique skill.

Because it cannot be upgraded, the Dark Hand ceases to be useful later in the game when higher-damage weapons become available. However, because it has high base Dark damage, it is very effective in the early game.

title: Humanity (item)
snippet:
A humanity is thought to be a fragment of the original Dark Soul, found by the Furtive Pigmy within the First Flame. They are present in every human from birth, and the presence of such a thing within a human being is the very distinctive element that differentiates a human from any other anthropomorphic creature present in the *Dark Souls* world. This could imply that humans are the only beings that possess two souls: one, the white Soul, is the essence of life as it is the energy of the First Flame, and the other, the dark one, a fragment of that very first, different Dark Soul.

This soul is made of dark, and therefore is immortal, does not lose its intensity when it is divided (most likely when part of it is transferred into a newly conceived baby), immunizes the carrier to the harming effects of the dark and, most importantly, is able to have feelings.

title: Divine (auxiliary effect)
snippet:
Divine (auxiliary effect) -  Dark Souls - item - effects 
 effects : A Divine infusion adds Magic damage to any given weapon as well as the Divine auxiliary effect. It also adds Faith scaling to weapons, while reducing Strength and Dexterity scaling.

The Divine Auxiliary Effect allows one to prevent Skeletons in The Catacombs and Tomb of the Giants from being resurrected. Without a Divine weapon, they will continually reanimate unless the Necromancer of the area is killed. Weapons with the Divine effect can also cause extra damage to specific enemies.

title: Self Augmentation
snippet:
Self Augmentation -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Self Augmentations, which can also be thought of as positive status effects, are temporary changes to the self that boost power and abilities. They can be granted by casting spells or using items, which last for their duration, or by wearing certain equipment, which last until they are removed.

In the case of spells and most items, augmentations cannot be canceled and only one can be active at a time. One must wait for the active augmentation to expire before applying a different one. However, it is possible to stack those with a limited duration with those that are gained by equipment.

title: Curse Jar
snippet:
Curse Jar -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - effects 
 effects : The Curse Jar releases a dark smoke that quickly inflicts curse status when the player stands near (this only affects the host of the world). These jars have a large spherical area of effect, allowing them to curse a player even if they are standing either on a floor above or below, coinciding with the respective location of the jar. If the curse meter suddenly starts building up and laughter can be heard, the player should quickly move away from that spot and scout the surroundings to determine the location of the jar.

title: Host of Embers
snippet:
Host of Embers -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - effects 
 effects : The Host of Embers mode acts in a similar way to how the Humanity mechanic was implemented in previous games.

Upon Restoring Ember, the player will gain a temporary boost to HP, increasing it by 30%. While in an area that has an active boss, many online features become active. The player may summon white phantoms, however they are also subject to invasion by dark spirits.

Ember status is lost upon player death.

title: Magic (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Magic (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - items_and_spells 
 items_and_spells : Certain defensive spells can increase Magic Defense, with varying results, but they cannot be stacked with each other. Only one spell can be active at a time. Small Blue Burrs are consumable items that can be purchased from Rosabeth of Melfia for 1200 souls each. Small Blue Burrs cannot be stacked with any of the defensive spells either. Consuming a Small Blue Burr will remove the Magic Defense provided by the spell, and apply the Small Blue Burr defense value.

The Strong Magic Shield sorcery can be cast on any shield to imbue it with Magic, similar to infusions. This grants the shield a 100% defense against all types of attacks (including Magic, physical, and some status effects) when blocking, however the effect is temporarily and the duration of the spell is dependent on the Intelligence stat.

title: Hard Leather Set (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Hard Leather Set (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - trivia 
 trivia : All pieces of the *Dark Souls III* variant provide Poise. This is in contrast to previous installments, which specifically noted that the helm was the only part to grant any Poise.
This set of armor is one of the few in the game where the female version is markedly different from the male version: the chest piece has a swath of gold-bordered red fabric on one arm, the boots are shiny with a grooved finish, and the helmet is a different shape.

title: Deep Gem
snippet:
Deep Gem -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : In order to unlock the Deep infusion for use, the player must first give the Sage's Coal to Blacksmith Andre.

Using a Deep Gem will infuse the target weapon with a deepened form of Dark, and in turn, will make a weapon deal both physical damage and dark damage, at an equal-split margin with one another.

Deep infusions also remove *all* scaling effects present on the weapon after infusion, much like a Fire Gem does, which means in order to achieve maximum damage on deep weapons, the player will have to fully-reinforce one.

title: Brightbug
snippet:
Brightbug -  Dark Souls II - item - usage 
 usage : When consumed, the player will deal 20% more damage and receive 20% less damage. Effects last for two minutes. Brightbugs cannot be used while a phantom or shade is present.

Brightbugs have a unique interaction when using it in combination with Sacred Oath. Casting Sacred Oath before using a Brightbug will stack the effects of the buffs, while reversing the order and using a Brightbug before casting Sacred oath will only give the effects of Sacred Oath. It seems that the effects of a Brightbug are not overridden by casting Sacred oath.

title: Cathedral Knight Greatshield
snippet:
The other main characteristic of the Cathedral Knight Greatshield is its high Dark defense, making it effective against attacks and spells of that nature. It is tied with Havel's Greatshield for the highest Dark defense among greatshields (only being beat by the Crest Shield, which is a medium shield), while having a significantly lower weight and Strength requirement. This makes it a very useful shield to face enemies in *Dark Souls III: The Ringed City*, particularly against Darkeater Midir, whose physical attacks deal partial Dark damage.

However, its non-Dark elemental absorption can be found wanting, as it is barely capable of blocking 60% of other damage types. When facing threats that are capable of dealing other types of elemental damage, it may be wise to rely on a different shield.

title: Parry and Riposte (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parry and Riposte (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - new_features 
 new_features : Listed below are some minor differences found in *Dark Souls II*, which may be slightly confusing to those who mastered these techniques in the original *Dark Souls* game.
In *Dark Souls II*, there is no temporary invincibility when parrying or riposting, but any damage received while performing these moves will be considerably less than normal (about 90% reduction).
The timing of a parry in *Dark Souls II* is different: it must be initiated when the enemy's attack animation begins, if parrying fast and medium weapons (daggers, straight swords, curved swords, etc.) or mid-swing, if parrying slow weapons (ultra greatswords, great hammers, etc.). In *Dark Souls*, parry had to be performed near the end of the animation (this difference, however, may not be very noticeable, it's more of a matter of personal preference).

title: Ruler's Sword
snippet:
Ruler's Sword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Ruler's Sword's damage scales uniquely with the amount of souls the player is currently holding. Depending on the player's stats, scaling may be negative until they've collected a significant amount of souls. The effect caps at one million (1,000,000) souls.

When fully upgraded and infused with an element, the weapon's attack rating can reach over 700 with a proper build and the relevant clutch ring, a relatively high number compared to most infused non-elemental weapons.
